 AIMIM president Owaisi seeks Centre's help for Indian pilgrims stranded in Makkah, Madina to return home
 SECTIONS AIMIM president Owaisi seeks Centre's help for Indian pilgrims stranded in Makkah, Madina to return home PTI Last Updated: Oct 22, 2026, 04:24:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Asaduddin Owaisi has highlighted the plight of 4,000 Indian pilgrims stranded in Makkah and Madina. Airlines have suspended flights due to a concerning security situation in Saudi Arabia. He urges the Indian government to arrange larger flights to facilitate their return. Owaisi emphasizes the abandonment of these pilgrims by their travel agents in this crisis. He calls for immediate action and support for the stranded individuals from relevant government officials.
 PTI AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi said 4,000 pilgrims from India are stuck in Makkah and Madina Hyderabad: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi on Thursday said 4,000 pilgrims from India are stuck in Makkah and Madina after airlines suspended flights to Saudi Arabian cities due to the security situation and urged the Centre to take measures for the pilgrims to return home.
 He said the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) must permit airlines to arrange flights in larger aircraft so that the stranded pilgrims can return to India.
 Also Read: India-US ties: Rubio says closer economic, energy cooperation benefits both nations 
Otherwise, "specified flights" must be arranged to bring them back, he said.
He sought the intervention of External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and other Union Ministers.
 Live Events
 "The Indian pilgrims have been abandoned by their travel agents. This needs your urgent intervention; in the meanwhile necessary support must be provided to the stranded pilgrims," he said.
 Also Read: France riots and India's protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar linked to same ecosystem, claims report 
 He tagged External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, Union Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju , Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu
Ram Mohan Naidu, and Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri in his post.
